label: Ōte-mon Gate

provenance.sourceEntity: Chiyoda City Tourism Association (Visit Chiyoda, official Chiyoda City tourism site)
provenance.evidence: The Imperial Household Agency's East Gardens visitor page names Ote-mon Gate as one of exactly three entrance and exit gates for the gardens and gives its walking times from Otemachi, Nijubashimae and Tokyo stations. The official Chiyoda City tourism site publishes a dedicated Ote-mon spot page describing it as the former main gate of Edo Castle, and that page's map block targets this coordinate for the gate itself. The agency's own access section (https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/visit/higashigyoen/index.html, re-consulted 2026-09-06) places this gate about a 5-minute walk from Otemachi Station exit C13a, about 10 minutes from Nijubashimae Station exit 6 on the Chiyoda Line, and about 15 minutes from JR Tokyo Station's Marunouchi north exit, documenting it as the point an approach from a local-transit station arrives at. Under the applicableContexts semantics recorded in TRANSIT_ACCESS_POINT_EVIDENCE.md the gate is therefore also a valid endpoint for an externally-originating trip whose local-transit leg ends in a short walk, so external-local-transit applies alongside external-walk. The coordinate and its Chiyoda City provenance are unchanged by that addition.

notes: Ordinal 001 records the order in which the Imperial Household Agency enumerates the three gates and carries no priority, preference or routing-selection meaning. Deliberately no default: the agency does not designate a preferred gate. external-local-transit was added by the Transit Access-Point Evidence Audit on 2026-09-06 on the Imperial Household Agency station-to-gate access evidence above; no default is claimed for that context either, so JP-029 resolves as ambiguous for transit exactly as it does for walking.

label: ASMUI Spiritual Hikes reception

provenance.evidence: The operator's own site separates reception, an internal shuttle bus and the hiking start point, stating that reception to the start point takes about 20-30 minutes, and it publishes a facility location coordinate for its address in Ginama, Kunigami, where reception and the visitor car park are. That published facility coordinate is used as the external arrival point. The Geospatial Information Authority of Japan's map annotation for the same facility falls about 100 m away, consistent with this location.

notes: External arrival/reception stage only. The hiking start point is a separate internal stage roughly 20-30 minutes further on and has no verifiable published coordinate, so no internal-hike trailhead record exists; external-local-transit is not claimed because no official source documents a transit endpoint here.
